title: Bin El Ouidane reservoir, 22 Jun to 21 Aug 2026
summary: From 22 Jun to 21 Aug 2026 the radar shows the lake shrinking from 31.35 km2 to 30.63 km2, while HH over the land rose slightly. The two dates are 60 days apart and span the NASA data gap, so the weeks between them are not seen.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: The lake changed by -0.72 km2, or -2.3%. Mean HV moved by -0.05 dB, but mean HH rose by 0.4 dB, and 2.13 km2 turned brighter in HH by more than 3 dB against 0.24 km2 darker. In HV, 0.58 km2 turned brighter and 0.34 km2 darker.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: Rough dry ground and fields had the largest brighter area in HH, 0.84 km2, and rose 0.42 dB on average. Trees, shrub and rugged slopes rose 0.37 dB in HH. The small changing fields type rose 0.9 dB in HV and 0.95 dB in HH.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause for the lake: summer drawdown for irrigation and evaporation; the dam's level and release records would confirm it. Possible cause for the higher HH: drier, rougher soil or stubble after the summer harvest. Possible cause: a small calibration difference between the two dates, since built-up land, which should not change, rose 0.49 dB in HH; stable targets on more dates would check it.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: Neither date carries a flag. NASA has no NISAR data from 27 Jul to 10 Aug 2026, so nothing between 16 Jul and 21 Aug 2026 is seen. Lake areas are approximate: 11.5% and 10.4% of the outline falls on land in the optical photo.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: Compare the 0.72 km2 loss with the dam's records for the same 60 days. Treat small HH changes with care until stable targets confirm them.
